pr_title: Fix crash in Vacuum:StatusesVacuum when deleting expired direct messages
pr_body:
Fixes #21210

Note that I am still **very** uncomfortable with that setting deleting unrecoverable posts (such as direct messages) mentioning local users.

issue_context.title: Error while running Vacuum::StatusesVacuum: private method `unlink_from_conversations' called for #<Status id:
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. Let the Vacuum scheduler run
2. Check the logs and see that the StatusesVacuum errored out
3.
...


### Expected behaviour

StatusesVacuum cleans old statuses

### Actual behaviour

A lot of old statuses to be cleaned up

### Detailed description

I have a single instance for testing things for the donte fork. I expected that after enabling the StatusesVacuum, my data usage was going to strongly decrease, but I was surprised to see it was not the case.
I started the vacuum with 3.33GB of postgres usage and 22.3GB of media storage. When it finished, media storage was down to 20.3GB and no significant change happened in the postgres usage.
I then opened a rails console and did the same query that the VacuumScheduler does to get statuses to remove and did a count, I still had `2130695` that matched the query.
Then, checking my logs, I found the error:
```
Nov 19 14:28:28 lond-com-br bash[3469320]: Error while running Vacuum::StatusesVacuum: private method `unlink_from_conversations' called for 
```

Since the vacuum scheduler is globbing down the errors and only printing, I guess this went unnoticed.

Maybe the vacuum scheduler could schedule jobs instead of running all schedulers and globbing the errors?

Also, does this method needs to be called, since it's already called in the before_destroy of the status model?

### Specifications

Mastodon 4.0.2-donte
Ruby 3.0.3
Node 14.19

I have questions:

Has calling the private method with `.each(&:unlink_from_conversations)` actually worked? (I mean with the original code?)

I doubt it did, because I tried it in the rails console:

```ruby

```

Calling the private method with `.send` is the working choice here, but [not the cleaner one](https://github.com/rubocop/ruby-style-guide#prefer-public_send).

But why do we need to call this private method anyway?

The [before_destroy hook](https://github.com/casaper/mastodon/blob/main/app/models/status.rb#L32) will call it anyway for us.

But this is not happening because the records are removed with `delete_all`:

https://github.com/casaper/mastodon/blob/main/app/lib/vacuum/statuses_vacuum.rb#L27

What would you think about using [destroy_all](https://api.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActiveRecord/Relation.html#method-i-destroy_all) instead?

```rb
Status.where(id: statuses.map(&:id)).destroy_all
```

This way the method would be called by the model itself.  
remove_from_account_conversations could be removed then.

And The comment in `vacuum_statuses!` mentioned that the media_attachments will remain orphaned.
But that requirement is met by the relation anyway:

https://github.com/casaper/mastodon/blob/main/app/models/status.rb#L70



I would see quite a few additional enhancements possible to this Vacuum::StatusesVacuum, especially regarding performance, but that would be quite out of scope here.

`analyze_statuses!` is never used. It should actually be removed.

https://github.com/casaper/mastodon/blob/main/app/lib/vacuum/statuses_vacuum.rb#L39-L41

> Has calling the private method with `.each(&:unlink_from_conversations)` actually worked? (I mean with the original code?)

No, and that's precisely what this PR fixes.

> But why do we need to call this private method anyway?

Because we are using `delete_all` instead of `destroy_all`. I assume that is for performance reasons, although the whole method is weird and seems to instantiate `Status` objects anyway.

> I assume that is for performance reasons, although the whole method is weird and seems to instantiate Status objects anyway.

I was guessing that too, but that failed on multiple layers:

1. statuses_scope causes the need of reinstantiating the batches again completely with `.select(:id, :visibility)`
2. statuses_scope does a subselect instead of `joins(:account)` 
3. remove_from_account_conversations maps the ids from the array, and does a new query on the model, with joins this time `.includes(:account, mentions: :account)`
4. remove_from_search_index maps out the ids again
5. the status model is queried again to perform delete_all
6. and delete_all is called with mapping out the ids again

We still target Ruby 2.6 (though that may change in the short-term future), which doesn't have support for that range notation.

1. you just need to make the range manually `nil...retention_period_as_id`
2. or if even that wouldn't work: `where('statuses.id < ?', retention_period_as_id)`

In any case,  that is readable, and not against the ORM. Safer, faster, more readable...
